claim: Which base the GRCh37 reference carries at SLC19A1 c.80, and therefore which direction the coding shorthand in methylation_panel.json must run to agree with the row's own p.His27Arg. No biological, statistical or clinical claim is asserted; in particular no claim is made about which rs1051266 allele affects folate transport, and the row's risk/ref dosage pair and genotype_effects categories are unchanged.
citations: dbSNP:rs1051266 (NCBI RefSNP v2, RefSeq NM_194255.4 / NP_919231.1) (accessed 2026-08-10)
high_stakes_two_source_rule: Engaged and satisfied. The reference-base claim is carried in a durable artifact (the rendered panel label), so it is backed by two sources that share neither a dataset nor an assertion chain: NCBI dbSNP/RefSeq and Ensembl GRCh37. They agree that the reference is 80A/His27 and the alternate 80G/Arg27. The His->Arg = A->G step itself is the standard genetic code and is not sourced.

queries.reduction_rule: Retained identity, merge status and every NM_194255.4 placement with its NP_919231.1 protein consequence. Dropped the other 24 transcripts, frequency studies, submissions and citations. Full response was 250974 bytes.
queries.result_used: rs1051266 is not merged. NM_194255.4:c.80= maps to NP_919231.1 residue 27 H->H, establishing His as the reference residue; NM_194255.4:c.80A>G maps to residue 27 H->R as a missense_variant.
queries.supports: A80G (His27Arg) is the reference-frame spelling; G80A is not.

queries.result_used: chr21:46,957,794 plus strand, allele_string T/C/G, ancestral_allele C, minor_allele C at MAF 0.4886. SLC19A1 is on the minus strand, so plus-strand T is coding A (reference) and plus-strand C is coding G (ancestral).
queries.supports: Independent confirmation of the reference base, and the explanation for the split literature naming: the reference carries the derived allele at this locus.

queries.service: local, read-only SQLite query against the repository working tree
queries.result_used: bundles/vep_bundle.db at origin/main 26cf641e reports ref=C alt=T hgvs_protein=p.Arg27His for rs1051266, contradicting both external sources. All 102254 of its single-base rows order ref alphabetically before alt with zero exceptions, so the columns are not reference/alternate and the derived hgvs_protein is inverted for the T/C class.
queries.supports: Nothing. Retained as the record of a contradicting in-repo artifact that must not be used as authority; written up separately.

source_versions_and_licenses._why: Recording the version/build and licence basis for every source, so a future auditor can establish which source state produced each retained payload and on what basis retaining it is permitted.

NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.version_or_build: Response carries the RefSNP's own last_update_build_id and dates; the 2026-08-10 access date bounds retrieval. No API version beyond the v0 path segment is issued.
NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.license_or_terms: US Government work produced by the National Library of Medicine; NCBI databases are in the public domain in the United States.
NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.retention_basis: Public domain. Only variant metadata for a single rsID is retained; no human subject data is involved.

Ensembl GRCh37 REST.version_or_build: GRCh37 archive endpoint. The response does not carry a release number, so the 2026-08-10 access date is the retrieval-version boundary. The GRCh37 site is a frozen mirror and lags current dbSNP, which is why dbSNP rather than Ensembl is the primary source for the identity and merge status of the rsID.
Ensembl GRCh37 REST.license_or_terms: Ensembl data are released under the Apache License 2.0.
Ensembl GRCh37 REST.retention_basis: Apache 2.0 permits redistribution with attribution. Only the single-rsID variation record is retained.

PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.version_or_build: Version of record. These are the three citations already carried by the panel row; only their titles are used here, and only as evidence of which spelling each uses.
PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.license_or_terms: Titles only, used as bibliographic fact. No abstract or full text is retained or reproduced.
PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.retention_basis: Bibliographic metadata, attributed by PMID. The titles were read from the repository's own tests/fixtures/pmid_metadata_snapshot.json rather than re-fetched.

corrections_and_retractions_checked: The three PMIDs are pre-existing citations on the row and are not the basis of any claim in this packet beyond which spelling their titles use; no claim of theirs is relied on, so no correction or retraction status could change a conclusion here. dbSNP was checked for a merge and reports rs1051266 as not merged.
privacy: No sample, genotype, or other personal data was read, transmitted or stored. Both external requests are single-rsID metadata lookups; the local query is read-only against a reference artifact.
